notes: The configuration database lives directly on the persistent partition now instead of on the RAM overlay with a background loop copying it down every few seconds -- that copying layer was behind a long run of real failures, and a commit is durable the moment it returns. Everything else still runs from RAM; WAL with synchronous=NORMAL keeps the write rate down. Reformatting the disk still snapshots the database to RAM and copies it back, and now closes the handle first so the unmount cannot fail. Restoring a backup closes the database before replacing the file and clears the WAL sidecars afterwards, so a log belonging to the old database cannot silently undo the restore. A client can no longer be pointed at a proxy that was deleted elsewhere, which used to answer 200 OK and leave the Proxy cell blank with no explanation. Missing form fields are marked in red where they are, with one message naming them all. The command log is copied to storage once a day so it survives a reboot. Bypass Proxy sits next to Proxy, and Logs moved to the end.
